title: The first and second neighborhood presentations and the three graph factors
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y a scheme morphism, c=(j:X→C,q:C→Y) a supplied open/proper compactification, and t=(a:X→U,e:U→P,p:P→Y) a proper/open/proper presentation, a≫e≫p=f [def-sf-etale-graph-word-projection]. Put T=P×_Y C, with projections p1,p2, v=(a≫e,j), O1=T×_C X and O2=T×_P U. Write b1,b2 for their open immersions in T, and s1=(v,id_X), s2=(v,a) for the graph lifts. They are proper: their composites with the separated second projections are respectively id_X and a. Define t1=(s1,b1,p1≫p) and t2=(s2,b2,p1≫p), presentations of f. Define B1: Rq_*Jj→t1.functor, B2:t.functor→t2.functor, and D:t1.functor→t2.functor to be exactly the existing locallyClosedGraphSide1, locallyClosedGraphSide2, and R(p1≫p)_* of locallyClosedGraphMiddle with its functor associators [lem-sf-etale-locally-closed-graph-model]. The specified graph comparison B is B1 ≪≫ D ≪≫ B2.symm. This merely displays the existing graph maps at presentation-functor endpoints; it chooses no new data.

proof.text: Construct v,s1,s2 by the existing pullback lifts. Their second projections are id_X and a. The second projections are separated by proper base change. Proper-to-separated cancellation gives properness of s1 and s2. Base change and composition give properness of p1≫p. The first projection equations prove that both words compose to f.

Use the existing three graph comparison constructions at these endpoints. Expand their definitions and reassociate the isomorphism hom components. The result equals sfGraphPresentationComparison componentwise, since it uses the same graph lifts, exchanges and compositors; differences between equality/properness witnesses are proof irrelevant. This proves the displayed factorization without a new tensor assertion.
